pretty.label: Output format
pretty.summary: Custom template (tformat:/format:) or a built-in pretty format
pretty.detail: tformat: and format: both take the template; they differ only in how entries are joined. The built-ins are NOT expressible as templates and are rendered by their own verified renderer.
gotchas: tformat: is terminator semantics (every entry ends with a newline); format: is separator semantics (newline between entries, none after the last). --format= means tformat:. Verified on the separator corpus family.
medium emits a 'Merge: a b' line on merge commits; raw emits one 'parent' line per parent and the gpgsig header verbatim. No template can do either.
raw does NOT emit the encoding header: git re-encodes for output and drops it. Verified on the explicit-encoding fixture commit.

email folds ASCII subjects at 78 columns and RFC 2047 Q-encodes non-ASCII ones into =?UTF-8?q?...?= words, breaking when a line would exceed 76. MIME headers appear when the message contains non-ASCII.
With a built-in, decoration defaults to auto, which is OFF unless stdout is a terminal. %d in a custom template always shows. Two different mechanisms.

abbrev.label: --abbrev
abbrev.detail: Applies uniformly to %h, %t and %p, and to the Merge: line of the built-ins.
gotchas: The fixture pins core.abbrev=7 so golden vectors are stable. On a real repository the default grows with object count, so a column layout aligned against %h will drift between repositories.
Verified: --abbrev=4 renders %h %t %p as 4 characters each; =16 as 16.

decorate.label: --decorate
decorate.detail: full uses complete ref names (refs/tags/v0.1.0); short strips the prefix.
gotchas: --decorate=no does NOT suppress %d in a custom template -- verified. It only removes decoration from the built-in formats. Only 'full' changes what %d renders.
auto is the default and is off when stdout is not a terminal, which is why the built-ins show no decoration in the corpus.

date.label: --date
date.summary: Format for %ad and %cd (and the Date: lines of the built-ins)
date.detail: Only %ad and %cd honor this. %aD, %ai, %as and the rest are fixed formats.
gotchas: relative and human styles are clock-dependent and cannot be pinned by a golden vector; they are host-supplied in the simulator.
relative and human are host-supplied here, like %ar and %ah: the sample records carry git's own rendering, captured when the record was extracted.

color.label: --color
color.detail: auto (git's default) colors when output is a terminal and not when piped. The preview is a terminal, so under auto it shows color. always forces color into pipes; never removes it.
gotchas: Under never, %Cred, %C(...) AND %Creset emit nothing at all. %C(always,...) forces emission regardless. Verified on 54 color vectors.
An invalid color spec is fatal in git: the whole git log aborts. Only specs that are emitted are checked, so under never an invalid spec goes unnoticed.

graph.label: --graph
graph.summary: Draw the commit graph to the left of each entry
graph.detail: Each entry's first line is prefixed by the commit row; every further line of the entry consumes one graph row. Implies topological order unless a date order is chosen.
gotchas: --graph with --reverse is fatal in git; turning one on turns the other off.
The '*' commit marker is never colored; only edges take column colors (log.graphColors). Verified on the graph-colors family.
A template ending in %n makes git print a padding row before the terminator, so the graph shows no gap.

order.label: order
order.detail: default is reverse committer-date walk order; with --graph it becomes topo.
gotchas: --date-order still never shows a parent before all of its children.

first_parent.label: --first-parent
first_parent.summary: Follow only the first parent of merge commits
first_parent.detail: Hides the commits merged in; the graph draws one edge per merge.
gotchas: Ordering still counts every parent: under --all, a branch tip that is a merge's second parent stays ordered as that merge's parent. Found by the graph corpus, not by reading.

reverse.label: --reverse
reverse.detail: Reverses the order of the walk.
gotchas: Cannot be combined with --graph: git exits with a fatal error.

abbrev_commit.label: --abbrev-commit
abbrev_commit.summary: Abbreviate the hash in the built-in formats' header
abbrev_commit.detail: Changes only the built-ins (commit <hash>, the oneline hash). A template's %H stays full.
gotchas: --oneline is --pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit. --pretty=oneline alone shows the FULL hash; the simulator once conflated them, and the corpus caught it.
